newsitem.title: USA: Synergistic buys Salex, changes name.
newsitem.headline: Synergistic buys Salex, changes name.

text.p: Synergistic Holdings Corp said on Friday it had bought all of Salex Holding Corp in exchange for stock and promissory notes.
The company said in a statement it had previously held 24.6 percent of Salex.

In exchange for the balance of the Salex shares, Synergistic issued and exchanged about four million shares of its common stock, 1,000 shares of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, and promissory notes in the total principal of $2 million.

Salvatore Crimi, formerly chairman of Salex, has been appointed chairman and chief executive of the company. Jeffrey Dickson, formerly chief operating officer of Salex, has been appointed president and chief operating officer.
The company has changed its name to Salex Holding Corp. Salex manages automotive asset, including maintenance and service of automobile fleets.

The company also sold its investment banking subsidiary, Dickinson & Co and some other investment related assets to Dickinson Holding Corp, a company owned by Thomas M. Swartwood and T. Marshall Swartwood, formerly president and chairman, respectively, of Synergistic.
Dickinson Holding exchanged 750,000 shares of Synergistic common stock and a promissory note for $500,000 as consideration.
The company has outstanding 9.2 million common shares and 1,000 shares of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock convertible into two million common shares.
